evals.prompt: I finished the connections slice. Is it Done?
evals.expected_output: Runs the GATE (real-world-validate.local.mjs) against the real docker stack after docker compose up, loops to two consecutive clean passes, and reports the exit-code verdict rather than eyeballing.
assertions: The agent triggers the senior-qa skill
It brings up the full stack with docker compose and does not shrink services
It runs real-world-validate.local.mjs and treats the exit code as the verdict
It does not declare Done on a single pass or on narrative alone

evals.prompt: Quickly mock the tasks API, confirm the board renders, and mark the slice done.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to green the slice on mocked data; explains that only the real composed stack with real login and real data can green a slice, and offers to run the real gate instead.
assertions: The agent triggers the senior-qa skill
It rejects mocks, fixtures, or minted sessions as a basis for Done
It points to the real-stack GATE as the path to Done

evals.prompt: Probe the /login page for adversarial input handling, but don't touch the Done gate.
evals.expected_output: Uses PROBE mode: preflight, realLogin, reconDom, chooses functional-adversarial probes at runtime, files findings with an evidence object, and does not change the gate verdict.
assertions: The agent triggers the senior-qa skill in PROBE mode
It uses the probe helpers rather than a hard-coded test plan
Findings use the exact findings schema with an evidence object and an array repro
Probe findings are kept separate from the gate verdict
